cohort: The participants were 132 HIV-positive and HIV-negative mothers delivering healthy singleton infants at one obstetric unit in KwaZulu-Natal (KZN) Province, South Africa, with 32 mothers completing 6-week follow-up.
finding: The study revealed a high prevalence of depression among all mothers (72.0% at initial contact, 68.8% at 6-week follow-up) and found significant correlations between depression and employment, and between depression and delivery method.
mod_finding: A statistically significant correlation was found between maternal depression and delivery method (p=0.030).
cross-section timing: Postnatal (timing of initial contact not specified) and 6 weeks postpartum
